summary.title: Why Software Engineers like Woodworking
summary.one_liner: A software engineer compares woodworking to programming, finding shared ideas like building your own tools, budgeting scarce resources, designing before building, and getting feedback from users.
takeaways: Building your own tools (woodworking 'jigs') parallels writing internal tooling in software.
Both fields require picking the right tool for each use case, which is hard when budgets are limited.
Scarce resources, including physical garage space and engineering time, need deliberate budgeting.
Sketching designs before building saves rework, and working on several projects at once can cover waiting time.
summary.summary: The author, a software engineer, describes taking up woodworking as a hobby with their toddler and notices how closely it resembles software engineering. The post walks through six parallels: building your own tools (jigs), choosing among many specialized tools, budgeting finite non-monetary resources such as garage space, designing before building, dealing with waiting (glue drying), and having users who request custom work. It ends by noting the one major difference is that you get to hold what you make, and that the author plans to keep programming. This is a short personal essay with no technical tutorial content.
